clue.text: Elements doing no good — time for a dire warning?

indicators.note: 'no good' asks for the letter that abbreviates good to be dropped from the word before it

blocks.note: acting is doing, performing
G is the usual abbreviation for good
the soothsayer warned Caesar to beware the Ides of March

explanation.surface: Some chemical elements are behaving badly, and it may be time to issue a grim warning about them.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ides of March was the date Caesar was told to beware, hence a time for a dire warning.
explanation.definitionFit: The actinides are a series of radioactive metallic elements in the periodic table, from actinium onwards.

clue.text: New deal underwritten by loveless Italian official

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so these letters take a fresh order
loveless means without love, the zero-shaped letter, so it is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
a Roman is an Italian
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A fresh deal signed off by an unromantic Italian official.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'underwritten by' means the first piece sits above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: An alderman is a senior member of a municipal council, a civic official.

clue.text: Spooner's awful solicitor is exhausted

indicators.note: named for Rev. Spooner, it asks for the opening sounds of two words to be swapped

blocks.note: dire is awful and a tout is someone who solicits custom; swap the D and T sounds

explanation.surface: A dreadful lawyer is worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' suggests a British lawyer, but here it is one who solicits, a tout.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired out means completely fatigued, which is exactly exhausted.

clue.text: Town shocked with foe moving around locality

indicators.note: letters moving around are shifted from their places into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A town is alarmed by an enemy prowling around the area.
explanation.definitionFit: Neck of the woods is an idiom for a particular area or neighbourhood, one's locality.

clue.text: Boat person travelling without purpose

blocks.note: first meaning: a fishing vessel using drift nets
second meaning: an aimless wanderer

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one boat person; split it after 'Boat' for two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a fishing vessel that works with drift nets and also someone who roams from place to place aimlessly.

clue.text: Old music maker with objection against wine

blocks.note: sack is an old name for a dry white wine such as sherry
a but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: An old musician who objects to drinking wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Against' means placed next to: the objection is put beside the wine, following it.
explanation.definitionFit: The sackbut is a Renaissance brass instrument, the forerunner of the trombone, so an old instrument.

clue.text: Zone being hit

blocks.note: first meaning: a region or strip
second meaning: to strike hard

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an area under attack; the two words are separate meanings joined by 'being'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means a region or strip of land; as a verb it is informal for striking someone hard.

clue.text: Provoke some felicitations

indicators.note: some means only part of the following word is wanted, a run of its letters

blocks.note: letters two to seven of the word

explanation.surface: Offering congratulations to stir up a reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit is to draw out or evoke a response, as to provoke one does.

clue.text: Restrict socialist in rows

blocks.note: to tie someone down is to restrict them
red is the traditional label for a socialist

explanation.surface: A socialist being restrained amid arguments, with rows read as quarrels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' tempts as quarrels, but it means ranked lines, as of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiered means arranged in layers or ranks one above another, which is set out in rows.

clue.text: Extremely well-disguised bouncer, a single being hit

indicators.note: something being hit is knocked about and smashed out of its usual shape

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: a batter hits a short-pitched bouncer for a single, while someone stays in disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bouncer is a short ball that rears up and a single is one run, so the surface evokes a batter at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone extremely well disguised cannot be recognised at all, so they are unrecognisable.

clue.text: English physicist — backward-looking character, one gathered

indicators.note: looking backward means the word is read from its end to its start
something gathered is taken in and enclosed by the word around it

blocks.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing person, a character
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A description of an English scientist as a nostalgic, sociable eccentric.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Dirac was the English theoretical physicist who shared the 1933 Nobel Prize for work on quantum mechanics.

clue.text: In bit of money I have to find motivation

blocks.note: taken as written
a cent is a small coin
the contraction I've

explanation.surface: Someone saying a little cash is what gets them going.
explanation.definitionFit: An incentive is something that spurs a person to act, the same thing as a motivation.

clue.text: British soldier newly decorated journalist ignored

indicators.note: something ignored is left out of the word it would otherwise be part of
done newly means made over in a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: A soldier has just received a medal, and the reporter covering it has been overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the journalist from 'decorated' and rearrange the remaining seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcoat was the historical nickname for a British infantryman, from the scarlet tunic of the uniform.

clue.text: Something hairy that bespeaks busy activity

blocks.note: first meaning: a tall, domed hairstyle of the 1960s
second meaning: a home for bees, figuratively any place of bustle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Something hairy' sounds like a frightening experience, but it is a hairdo.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a towering bouffant hairstyle and also a hive of bees, a stock image of a place full of industrious work.

clue.text: Debasement of grown-up needs mate finally helping

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: an adult is a grown-up
the last letter of mate
a ration is a portion or helping

explanation.surface: A grown-up who needs a pal's help sounds like a story of someone being degraded.
explanation.definitionFit: Adulteration is the lowering of quality by mixing in inferior substances, a form of debasement.

clue.text: Knowing how to figure things out?

definitions.text: Knowing how to figure things out?

blocks.clueFragment: Knowing how to figure things out?
blocks.note: surface reading: able to solve puzzles or work out problems
setter's reading: figures are numbers, so this is being competent with arithmetic

explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure out' suggests reasoning in general, but figures are digits, so the clue means skilled with numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Being numerate is the numerical counterpart of literacy: having basic competence in calculation.

clue.text: We American guys can miss out 'u' in this!

definitions.text: We American guys can miss out 'u' in this!

indicators.note: to miss out a letter is to leave it absent from the word that holds it

blocks.note: taken as written
buster is American slang for a man or fellow
the letter itself

explanation.surface: An American exclaiming that their dictionary lets them drop the u from words like colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: Webster's dictionary, Noah Webster's work, set American spellings such as color and honor.
explanation.definitionFit: Webster's is the standard American dictionary, whose spellings omit the u found in British honour and colour.

clue.text: A daring exploit, maybe

blocks.note: per means 'a', as in so much per day
an adventure is a bold, risky undertaking

explanation.surface: Someone guessing that something might be a bold escapade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' looks like a mere article but stands for PER, as in 'thirty miles an hour'.
explanation.definitionFit: Peradventure is an archaic adverb meaning perhaps, by chance, so it can replace maybe.

clue.text: Report of a tree worker being suspended

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the words are taken by their sound

blocks.note: a bay is a laurel tree and an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: News of a forestry employee being laid off pending inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tree worker' suggests a lumberjack, but it is an insect on a laurel.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeyant means in abeyance, temporarily inactive or held over, which is being suspended.

clue.text: Five narrow streets — they may have water flowing through them

definitions.text: they may have water flowing through them

blocks.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
alleys are narrow lanes

explanation.surface: A description of five narrow lanes that flood, such as in Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Valleys are low land between hills, which typically have a river or stream running along them.

clue.text: People's ordeal — bishop intervenes

definitions.note: possessive; the answer is an adjective, of a people

indicators.note: to intervene is to come between, so this letter goes inside the other word

blocks.note: a trial is a painful ordeal
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A community's suffering, in which a bishop steps in to help.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribal means belonging to a tribe, that is, to a people, as the possessive does.

clue.text: Perhaps key is put down

blocks.note: taken as written
to land a plane is to put it down

explanation.surface: Perhaps a crucial thing is being set aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like a door key or something crucial, but a key or cay is a low island, as in the Florida Keys.
explanation.definitionFit: A key is a small low island or reef, so it is one example of the answer, as 'perhaps' signals.

clue.text: Bring back stock again

blocks.note: first meaning: return something to a former state
second meaning: put into storage once more

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense needs the word split as re- plus store.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to reinstate or return something, and split as a prefix plus verb it means to lay in supplies a second time.

clue.text: Tenants more trouble, we hear?

indicators.note: what we hear is the sound of the words, not their spelling

blocks.note: more trouble means less ease, less comfort

explanation.surface: A landlord grumbling that tenants are more hassle than they are worth.
explanation.definitionFit: Lessees are those who hold a property under a lease, which is what tenants do.

clue.text: Go, say, with directors showing enthusiasm

blocks.note: a company's directors form its board
to be game is to be willing and keen

explanation.surface: Reads like an instruction to set off with the bosses keenly on side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like a verb, but it is the Japanese strategy game played with stones on a grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Go is played on a board, so it is an example of the category; 'say' marks it as one instance.

clue.text: Clamour created by ex-PM in speech

indicators.note: in speech means as the name is said out loud rather than written

blocks.note: Tony Blair, British Prime Minister 1997-2007

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister causing an uproar with one of his speeches.
explanation.definitionFit: A blare is a loud harsh noise, close in sense to a clamour or din.

clue.text: Youngster with male chromosome is not male!

definitions.note: describes a woman rather than naming one

blocks.note: a lad is a boy
the Y chromosome is the one carried only by males

explanation.surface: A paradox: a boy with a male chromosome turns out not to be male at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that adding the male Y to a boy produces a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady is a woman, someone who is by definition female rather than male.

clue.text: Suffering from Covid, maybe, being flat

blocks.note: first meaning: unable to taste, a known symptom of Covid
second meaning: dull and insipid

explanation.walkthrough: Loss of taste was a widely reported Covid symptom; 'flat' is the everyday sense of dull or bland.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes food without flavour and, literally, a person who cannot sense taste; flat is a synonym for insipid.
